job.style: a description of a classroom activity or experiment and what it shows

response.passage: In our science class today, we explored how our bodies respond to physical activity. We started with a gentle warm-up, which prepares our muscles and heart for harder work, reducing the risk of injury. During the session, we learned that muscles do not actually grow while we are lifting weights or doing push-ups. Instead, the muscle fibers develop tiny tears during exercise, and they grow back stronger and larger only during the rest periods that follow. We also discussed that strength exercise is not just for bodybuilders; simple bodyweight movements like squats or push-ups help everyone build functional strength. Furthermore, we examined the myth that sweating is fat leaving the body. In reality, sweating is just our body’s way of cooling down to maintain a healthy temperature. Finally, we learned that to keep improving, we must gradually increase the difficulty of our workouts, because doing the same easy exercise forever will eventually stop challenging our muscles. We concluded that consistent, varied movement combined with proper recovery is the key to a healthy body, rather than relying on quick fixes or extreme measures.
response.summary: This lesson explains that muscles grow during rest rather than during exercise. It also clarifies that sweating is for cooling the body and that progressive difficulty is necessary for fitness.
